culture_narrative: Employs approximately 12K people. Revenue per employee of $306K ranks in the below the sector median among Industrials peers. Each employee generates $22K of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $2K per employee reflects an ownership culture. CEO compensation is 14× revenue per employee (reasonable relative to workforce productivity). Governance score flags elevated compensation governance risk (9/10).
financial_summary: INPOST S.A. is a mid-cap industrials business with a $9.0B market cap on $3.7B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +35% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.

Returns on capital run at 13% against a 7% cost of capital, a 6-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it. Gross margins of 65% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $260M in free cash flow — roughly 7 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 5.20× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 2.4× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and interest coverage runs at 3.3×.
Shareholder yield is only 0.1%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 99% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.
